hypothesis: ML can rank Donchian breakout quality well enough to filter the weak ones and clear costs
reason: Ranking skill is real and strongly validated (z=+9.70 against a permutation null, seed sd 0.0010), but worth only +0.15 pts/trade against a 2.50 pt round turn. Break-even cost multiple 1.05, so a 5% cost increase kills it. Fails the matched control at p=0.080. P&L is concentrated in the final third of the research block (-1.74/+0.29/+1.89), the one-lucky-window signature.
learned: Statistically significant predictive skill and an economically usable edge are different things. The permutation test is what makes this claim safe to state: without it, AUC 0.578 would have looked like either a triumph or a leak, and there would have been no way to tell.

hypothesis: The authentic Donchian mechanic - a resting stop order AT the channel level - beats entering at the next bar's open after a close beyond it. CLAUDE.md calls the entry mechanic the biggest lever found on this branch.
method: paired: identical triggers, identical geometry, identical exit walk; only the fill differs. Needs no control. Corrects an earlier run that scored the stop-entry book against a next-open matched control, which was mismatched to the mechanic.
best_cell: n_entry=10, stop 2.0 ATR, targ 2.0 ATR, exp -0.78 pts/trade
decision: REAL MECHANISM, DOES NOT RESCUE THE FAMILY
reason: The stop order genuinely fills 2.2-2.6 points better than the next open, which is the size of the whole round turn. But that improvement is only retained when the stop is wide: the paired difference is monotone increasing in stop multiple and monotone decreasing in channel length, from -4.07 (n=40, stop 1.5) to +2.36 (n=10, stop 2.5). Entering earlier puts you in the noise the confirmation bar would have filtered, so a tight stop gives back more than the fill gained. Best configuration still loses 0.78 pts/trade.
learned: A better fill is not the same as a better trade. The mechanic interacts with the stop, and reporting either one alone would have been misleading in opposite directions.

hypothesis: The Donchian breakout has a gross directional edge that transaction costs destroy
reason: Gross expectancy with costs and slippage switched off is NEGATIVE at every entry lookback tested (-0.30 to -1.00 pts/trade), and gross excess over a cost-free matched control is approximately zero (z from -0.60 to +0.16). The rule loses money at a round turn of zero.
learned: This is not an edge destroyed by costs - there is no gross edge to destroy. That distinction matters because it rules out every standard remedy at once: a cheaper venue, a larger contract, a wider barrier or a longer hold all scale the signal and the cost together, and the signal is zero. Directional edge and ranking skill are also different things: the ML agent found real ranking skill (AUC 0.578) on a population with no directional edge.

hypothesis: The no-gross-edge finding is specific to NAS and will not replicate on US30
reason: Gross expectancy per unit ATR is negative on both instruments at 9 of 10 lookbacks, clustered tightly in -0.026 to -0.088 ATR, and gross excess over a cost-free matched control is insignificant everywhere (all p > 0.17). The single positive cell, US30 at n=80, is one of ten tested, has p=0.173, and still loses 1.99 pts net. NAS and US30 agree to three decimals at n=20 (-0.026 ATR each) despite their breakout events overlapping at only Jaccard 0.26.
learned: The absence of gross edge is structural to the Donchian breakout in this window, not an artefact of one instrument, one feed or one cost model. Expressing the result per unit ATR is what makes the two instruments comparable - in raw points US30's numbers look 2-3x worse purely because its ATR is 2.4x larger.

hypothesis: A pre-window trend-strength reading (ADX(14) at 07:00) gates which sessions the Donchian breakout should be traded in
rule: Trade the n=20 Donchian breakout in 07:00-11:00 NY only on sessions whose ADX(14) at the 07:00 bar exceeds 30. Stop 1.5 ATR, target 2.0 ATR, one trade per session.

passes.circular_shift_calibration: shifted meaningless states pass at 6.1% vs 5% nominal
passes.jackknife: gap survives all 7 leave-one-year-out drops, +2.96 (drop 2022) to +5.60 (drop 2020)
passes.structural_coherence: present at n_entry>=20, absent at n_entry=10, on BOTH instruments
passes.leakage: dropping the 07:00 bar itself changes nothing (excess +5.50 -> +5.12)

fails.parameter_stability: modal threshold kept in only 32-48% of folds
fails.multiplicity: 238 configurations gated; Bonferroni threshold 2.1e-4, circular-shift p=0.0006 does not clear it
fails.shape: a STEP at ADX 30, not a gradient - the agent's own disjoint-bucket test showed the cumulative sweep's monotonicity was a tail artefact

reason: The in-sample effect is real: it is not leakage, not one year, not one instrument, and it survives a circular-shift control designed for an autocorrelated session-level state at p=0.0006. But when the threshold must be CHOSEN from data available at the time and re-chosen as the window rolls, median out-of-sample expectancy is negative in two of three walk-forward configurations, fewer than half the folds are profitable, and the modal threshold survives re-selection in only 32-48% of folds. The Monte Carlo bootstrap CI on expectancy includes zero.
learned: A statistically real conditional effect and a harvestable edge are different things. Every static test this candidate passed - control, jackknife, cross-instrument sign, leakage - conditions on knowing the threshold. Walk-forward is the only test that charges for having to discover it, and that is exactly what the effect could not survive. It also corrects two of my own earlier readings: the 2022 concentration was an artefact of reading gate-arm year slices instead of the jackknife, and the monotone threshold sweep was a tail artefact the agent's disjoint-bucket test exposed.

hypothesis: The walk-forward failure of the ADX gate is caused by threshold SELECTION noise rather than by instability of the effect itself
reason: Fixing the threshold a priori instead of re-selecting it every fold materially improves the picture: 60-67% of contiguous out-of-sample blocks are positive and the gap over baseline is positive in 67-70% of them, with median gap +1.67 to +2.75. The ordering of thresholds also transfers across the two halves of the research block - high thresholds earn and low ones lose in both. So the walk-forward failure was substantially a selection-noise problem, not purely an unstable effect. But 4 of 6 positive blocks is binomial p ~ 0.34, expectancy is negative at twice the modelled cost, and the effect is markedly stronger in the second half of research (+4.18 vs +0.44 at ADX>30), which is regime concentration adjacent to the locked block rather than evidence of robustness.
learned: Walk-forward conflates two failure modes and it is worth separating them. A re-selection walk-forward charges for discovering the parameter; a fixed-parameter rolling test charges only for the effect persisting. When the first fails and the second does not, the honest description is 'a real effect too noisy to tune', not 'no effect'.

hypothesis: If the ADX@07:00>30 gate is a real mechanism rather than a tuned number, it should transfer to US30 unchanged
method: threshold FIXED at 30 a priori, never retuned per instrument; gate applied to triggers and the book re-simulated
decision: STRONGEST CANDIDATE - earns the single holdout look
reason: With the threshold fixed and never retuned, all six gaps at n_entry>=20 are positive across two instruments whose breakout events overlap at only Jaccard 0.23-0.28, and both instruments fail identically at n_entry=10. Six same-sign results is p~0.016 under a no-effect null, though the tests are not fully independent. The gated and ungated trade populations are structurally near-identical on ATR, channel width, break distance, time of day and side mix, so the gate is not selecting different breakouts - it is selecting the days on which breakouts pay, which is an interpretable mechanism rather than a fitted artefact.
still_fails: re-selection walk-forward (median OOS negative in 2 of 3 configurations), expectancy negative at 2x cost, US30 p-values individually weak (0.22, 0.107, 0.043), effect stronger in the second half of the research block
learned: Fixing a parameter a priori and shipping it unchanged to a second instrument is a far stronger test than any in-sample statistic. It cannot be tuned, so a positive result is not selection. This is the evidence that moved the candidate from rejected to holdout-worthy.

hypothesis: ADX@07:00>30 is a volatility gate in disguise; a matched-selectivity ATR gate will reproduce it and ATR is the simpler explanation
decision: HYPOTHESIS DISPROVEN - ADX is not a volatility proxy, and the mechanism sharpens
reason: ADX@07:00 and the causal trailing ATR percentile at 07:00 are essentially uncorrelated (0.057 NAS, 0.052 US30). A matched-selectivity volatility gate is strongly NEGATIVE on both instruments (-3.82 and -6.29 excess), so high volatility is bad for these breakouts rather than good. The strongest cell on both instruments is ADX>30 combined with LOW ATR percentile: +6.46 excess at p=0.0000 and 50.2% win rate on NAS, +7.87 excess at p=0.0633 on US30. The worst cell is high ATR with low ADX: -8.14 excess and a 36.9% win rate.
learned: Two things. First, the mechanism is 'trending but not volatile' - directional persistence with contained range is when a breakout continues rather than whipsaws, which is textbook trend-following rather than a mined artefact. Second, a methodological correction to my own earlier note: comparing raw ATR LEVELS between gated and ungated populations was misleading because ATR level drifts upward with index price over a nine-year sample. The causal trailing percentile is the right measure and it shows no association at all.
